title: How the Dirty Set Moves: Characterizing Schedule Reuse in Incremental Sparse Matrix Multiplication
summary: In incremental sparse matrix multiplication, only a few input rows change per step, and we call those rows the dirty set. A direct column-wise incremental update beats a tiled executor that keeps its preparation and cached schedules in 779 of 837 workloads, and it is 2.1-8.2x faster than the best of eight full-recomputation codes. Tiling only pays off when tiles merge many entries into each output write.

title: TLA+-Bench: An Execution-Grounded Benchmark and Dataset for Natural-Language to TLA+ Specification Generation
summary: We built a benchmark that checks generated specifications by running them. It contains 403 model-checked specifications and 897 parse-only specifications from 13 public repositories. On a fixed set of model outputs, changing the grading rules moves the measured correctness rate from 10.0% to 1.7%. The paper makes those choices explicit so that a reported score says what was actually checked.

title: TLA-Prover: Verifiable TLA+ Specification Synthesis via Preference-Optimized Low-Rank Adaptation
summary: We trained a 20-billion-parameter model to generate TLA+ specifications, using supervised fine-tuning followed by repair-based reinforcement learning with TLC feedback. The paper reports 9 of 30 held-out problems passing both model checking and the Diamond check, which tests whether an altered invariant produces a violation. These are results for the paper's benchmark and evaluation procedure; they do not establish correctness on arbitrary systems.

title: Can LLMs Write Correct TLA+ Specifications? Evaluating Natural-Language-to-TLA+ Generation
summary: We evaluated 30 language models against a corpus of 205 TLA+ specifications, checking their output with SANY and TLC. The study found a substantial gap between producing valid syntax and satisfying the modeled properties: the best reported rates were 26.6% and 8.6%, respectively. Larger models did not consistently do better. This evaluation motivated the later work on verifier feedback during training.
